This folder holds the primary task models and the script that produces our test-set predictions. Run everything from the project root (open `module2-claims.Rproj`).

## Files

| File | What it is | Owner |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| `scripts/task4/headers-test.R` | Phase 1: tests paragraphs-only vs paragraphs + headers | Binary (4a) |
| `scripts/task4/binary-model-development-task4A.R` | Model comparison, final fit, saves the binary model | Binary (4a) |
| `scripts/task4/bclass-functions.R` | Cleaning, TF-IDF and `predict_bclass()` | Binary (4a) |
| `results/bclass-model.rds` | Saved binary model (lasso) | Binary (4a) |
| `scripts/task4/multiclass-model-development-task4B.R` | Model comparison, final fit, saves the multiclass model | Multiclass (4b) |
| `scripts/task4/mclass-functions.R` | Defines `predict_mclass()` and `predict_mclass_relevant()` | Multiclass (4b) |
| `results/multiclass-comparison.RData` | 10-split comparison results | Multiclass (4b) |
| `results/mclass-model.rds` | Saved multiclass model (lasso) | Multiclass (4b) |
| `scripts/task4/predict-test.R` | Loads both models, predicts the test pages, saves `pred_df` | Shared |
| `results/preds-group2.RData` | Final predictions (Deliverable 3), created by the script | Shared |

## How to run

Restart R, then source the prediction script:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
source('scripts/task4/predict-test.R')
```

It only saves `results/preds-group2.RData` when every check passes. Until the multiclass files exist, it warns and does not save.

## multiclass side needs

1.  **`results/mclass-model.rds`**: the fitted model, saved with `saveRDS()`. Include everything needed to score new pages (vocabulary, IDF weights, any PCA loadings, the fit itself).
2.  **`scripts/task4/mclass-functions.R`**: defines `predict_mclass(model, df)`.

`predict_mclass()` must follow this contract:

- **Input:** a data frame with `.id` and `text_tmp` (raw HTML), like `claims_test`
- **Output:** a tibble with `.id` and `mclass.pred`
- **`mclass.pred`:** a factor with exactly these levels, in this order: `'N/A: No relevant content.'`, `'Physical Activity'`, `'Possible Fatality'`, `'Potentially unlawful activity'`, `'Other claim content'`
- **One row per input page, no `NA`s.** Give pages you can't parse a fallback label instead of dropping them.

A starting skeleton:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# scripts/task4/mclass-functions.R
predict_mclass <- function(model, .df){
  cl <- clean_pages(.df)          # reuse the binary cleaning, or your own
  # ... build features with your saved vocabulary / loadings ...
  # ... predict with model$fit, take the most likely class ...
  tibble(.id = cl$.id,
         mclass.pred = factor(pred_labels, levels = model$levels))
}
```

`clean_pages()`, `tokenize_pages()`, `build_vocab()` and `make_dtm()` are already loaded from `bclass-functions.R` when the prediction script runs, so you can reuse them.

## N/A rule

In the training data, `mclass` is N/A exactly when `bclass` is N/A. The script prints how many test pages the two models disagree on. Pick one rule and uncomment it in section 4 of `predict-test.R`:

- **(a)** the binary model decides N/A
- **(b)** the multiclass model decides N/A

**Chosen: rule (a).** Multiclass N/A-vs-not accuracy was 0.786, below the binary model's 0.806, so the binary model decides N/A. Rule (a) was extended to cover both directions: when the binary model says Relevant but the multiclass model says N/A, `mclass.pred` is set to the multiclass model's most likely non-N/A class (`predict_mclass_relevant()`). This fixed 108 test pages where the two columns disagreed (30 one way, 78 the other), so `pred_df` now has no contradictions.

## Binary model at a glance

- **Text:** paragraphs + headers (h1 to h6), cleaned; non-HTML pages get the N/A fallback
- **Features:** word TF-IDF, words on 5+ training pages (about 6,800)
- **Model:** lasso logistic regression (glmnet), penalty chosen by cross-validation
- **Held-out performance (10 splits):** accuracy 0.806, ROC AUC 0.864, sensitivity 0.788, specificity 0.826

# Binary model (task 4a): notes for Deliverable 2

## Preprocessing

Paragraph and header (h1-h6) text was scraped from each page's HTML, then cleaned: URLs, emails, punctuation, digits and symbols removed; lowercased; stop words removed; words lemmatized. Pages that weren't HTML (JSON, PDFs, scraper errors) get the fallback label N/A. Text was represented as TF-IDF over words appearing on at least 5 training pages (about 6,800 words).

## Method

Lasso logistic regression (glmnet, alpha = 1), with the penalty chosen by 10-fold cross-validation. Chosen after comparing 7 models on the same 10 random 80/20 splits: PCA logistic regression (in-class baseline), lasso, elastic net, ridge, lasso with bigrams, and two RBF SVMs. All reached about 80% accuracy; lasso tied for best and was the simplest to deploy. The final model was refit on all 2,146 HTML training pages.

## Results (held-out, mean over 10 splits; positive class = Relevant)

| Metric      | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Sensitivity | 0.788 |
| Specificity | 0.826 |
| Accuracy    | 0.806 |
| ROC AUC     | 0.864 |

Comparison: baseline PCA logistic regression reached 0.800 accuracy. Adding headers left accuracy unchanged but raised AUC (0.864 vs 0.847). Neural networks were not pursued (software setup issues).

## Multiclass model at a glance

- **Text and features:** same as the binary model (paragraphs + headers, word TF-IDF on words appearing on 5+ training pages, about 6,800 words)
- **Model:** multinomial lasso regression (glmnet), penalty chosen by cross-validation
- **Held-out performance (10 splits):** accuracy 0.779, macro sensitivity 0.662, macro specificity 0.927

# Multiclass model (task 4b): notes for Deliverable 2

## Preprocessing

Same pipeline and TF-IDF features as the binary model. Pages that weren't HTML get the fallback label N/A.

## Method

Multinomial lasso regression (glmnet, alpha = 1) over the 5 classes, with the penalty chosen by 10-fold cross-validation. Chosen after comparing 3 models on the same 10 random 80/20 splits (stratified by class): PCA multinomial regression (in-class baseline), lasso and elastic net. Lasso and elastic net tied (difference within split noise); lasso was chosen to match the binary model. The final model was refit on all 2,146 HTML training pages. For the test predictions, the binary model decides N/A vs relevant and the multiclass model picks the claim type (see N/A rule above).

## Results (held-out, mean over 10 splits; sensitivity and specificity macro-averaged over the 5 classes)

| Metric      | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Sensitivity | 0.662 |
| Specificity | 0.927 |
| Accuracy    | 0.779 |

Comparison: baseline PCA multinomial regression reached 0.771 accuracy and 0.617 macro sensitivity. Sensitivity is lowest for the smallest class ("Other claim content", 100 training pages, 0.27) and highest for N/A and Possible Fatality (0.85).
